extras.name: full
extras.purpose: All seven ecosystem components with compatible version ranges.

extras.name: governance
extras.purpose: Policy-as-code, audit evidence, and portable semantic contracts. Already part of the default install; the extra exists as an explicit, documented request.

extras.name: local
extras.purpose: Local-first private deployment stack. Pulls FastAPI and Uvicorn, and expects local Ollama, PostgreSQL, and Docker at runtime.

extras.name: observability
extras.purpose: Measurement plus OpenTelemetry export. Pulls the OTLP gRPC exporter chain (grpcio, protobuf).

components.name: AgentForge
components.purpose: Async multi-agent orchestration with model routing, budget caps, RBAC, tool sandboxing, policy rules, pluggable memory, and a hash-chained audit trail.
components.notes: Runs fully offline through a deterministic echo provider with zero configuration. ModelSwapBench and PrivateAIStack both depend on this distribution at runtime. Hosted provider SDKs and pgvector are opt-in extras of agentforge-oss and are not installed by this suite.

components.name: AgentPolicyPack
components.purpose: Deterministic, fail-closed policy-as-code evaluation for agent actions, with bundle validation, embedded policy tests, simulation, and conservative diffing.
components.notes: Evaluates policy decisions and returns obligations, limits, and evidence. The calling system remains responsible for enforcing every decision.

components.name: AIAuditLog
components.purpose: Vendor-neutral tamper-evident audit-event envelope with RFC 8785 canonical JSON, SHA-256 hash chains, checkpoints, optional Ed25519 signatures, and privacy profiles.
components.notes: Hash chaining is tamper-evident, not immutable storage or external anchoring. Signatures prove key possession and byte integrity, not real-world identity or legal non-repudiation. Pulls the cryptography wheel.

components.name: AIMeter
components.purpose: Decimal-precise measurement of AI usage, provider and infrastructure cost, allocation, outcomes, and budgets, reported as cost per successful outcome.
components.notes: Missing pricing is reported as unknown and never treated as zero. Calculated cost is not invoice-confirmed, projected savings are not realized savings, and budgets are evaluated rather than enforced. Previously published as openaimeter; the ai_meter import package is current.

components.name: ModelSwapBench
components.purpose: Repeatable model portability and replacement benchmarking with deterministic evaluators, cost-per-success economics, vendor-exit reports, and per-task routing plans.
components.notes: Depends on agentforge-oss at runtime, but its Forge adapter exercises the provider layer only, not full supervisor or tool orchestration. The default deterministic provider needs no credentials and no model downloads. Hosted providers are denied unless explicitly enabled. The checked api_symbols, including the gate helpers evaluate_gate and GateThresholds, are present across the whole supported range (0.1.0b1 and later).

components.name: OpenOntologyLite
components.purpose: Executable semantic contracts for organizational entities, relationships, actions, and permissions, plus AI System Maps recording workload risk, allowed model routes, and review expectations.
components.notes: Executable means deterministic validation and contract transformation. It does not execute actions, enforce authorization, route models, or perform general-purpose inference.

components.name: PrivateAIStack
components.purpose: Local-first FastAPI service and deployment template combining Ollama, Forge orchestration, PostgreSQL-backed document memory, governed static code review, and JSONL audit records.
heavy_infrastructure: PostgreSQL with pgvector for persistent document memory
Docker and Docker Compose for the packaged deployment template
optional_infrastructure: OpenTelemetry Collector and Jaeger for tracing
components.notes: Installing the distribution pulls FastAPI and Uvicorn but starts no service. The runtime services above are never installed or started by this suite. Task and review registries are in-process, and packaged defaults are development values that require hardening before operational use. The Python import package exposes only __version__.
